summary: Tsuzuki proves the dual form of Kedlaya's minimal slope conjecture for overconvergent F-isocrystals on curves (Corollary 6.5), and for overconvergent Q̄_p-F-isocrystals on smooth varieties over finite fields up to the compatibility with the given morphism (Theorem 7.20). The tools are PBQ filtrations, saturation and de Jong's opposite filtrations. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed, and twenty-four findings are recorded against arXiv v3. After review none affects a stated result: the literal slips in Theorems 3.12, 3.19, Proposition 3.18 and Definition 7.14 have clear intended forms, and the circular proof of Lemma 3.31 is repaired. Not formalised.

items.statement: The generic-disc solvability and boundedness conditions are unchanged by admissible changes of local or generically étale coordinates.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Closure under abelian tensor operations
items.statement: The solvable subcategory and the bounded subcategory of differential modules are each abelian and closed under tensor products and duals. This does not imply that every solvable object is bounded, nor closure of bounded objects under arbitrary extensions.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Detection of generic solution conditions after local extension
items.statement: For Mη over Eη, solvability or boundedness holds iff it holds after extension to Eα.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Frobenius supplies solvability
items.statement: Every φ–∇ module over Eη or Eα is solvable on its generic open unit disc.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Unit-root Frobenius supplies boundedness
items.statement: A unit-root φ–∇ module over Eη or Eα is bounded on its generic disc.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Boundedness equivalent to slope splitting
items.statement: A φ–∇ module over Eη or Eα is bounded iff its Frobenius slope filtration splits as a direct sum of pure differential Frobenius modules. For Eα this is CT11 over perfect residue field; generic descent additionally uses Lemma 3.11.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Descent intersection after perfected generic extension
items.statement: Inside the common extended local field, Eη equals the intersection of its completed perfection extension with Eα. This descends the uniquely specified off-diagonal Frobenius splitting matrix from the two coefficient fields.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Maximally bounded quotient
items.statement: For nonzero solvable M over B, define M^b as the smallest differential submodule with bounded quotient; M/M^b is nonzero and every bounded quotient factors uniquely through it. For φ–∇ M the kernel is Frobenius stable. Extend the construction on zero by zero, separately from the nonzero assertion.

items.statement: (Eα⊗EηMη)^b=Eα⊗EηMη^b as φ–∇ submodules; equivalently the maximal bounded quotient commutes with this base change.

items.name: Pure of bounded quotient
items.statement: A nonzero φ–∇ module is PBQ if its maximal bounded quotient is pure. Its slope equals the maximal slope of the original module. Treat zero separately, not as an object with a unique slope.

items.name: Same-slope PBQ direct sums
items.statement: A direct sum of PBQ φ–∇ modules having the same maximal slope is PBQ. Different maximal slopes are excluded.

items.name: Nonzero quotients preserve PBQ and maximal slope
items.statement: If M is PBQ and M→N is a surjection with N≠0, then N is PBQ and λmax(N)=λmax(M).

items.name: PBQ detected by nonzero unit-root tensoring
items.statement: For a nonzero unit-root N and nonzero M, M is PBQ iff M⊗N is PBQ; (M⊗N)/(M⊗N)^b≅(M/M^b)⊗N. The nonzero condition on N is necessary.

items.name: Generic PBQ filtration
items.statement: For M, form the unique increasing finite filtration 0=P₀⊂…⊂P_r=M such that G_i=P_i/P_(i−1) is PBQ and λmax(G_i) strictly decreases. P₁ is the maximally PBQ submodule in the source's sense. The slopes are those of G_i, not P_i.

items.name: Bounded quotient from graded PBQ top quotients
items.statement: For G_i=P_i/P_(i−1), the bounded quotient M/M^b is isomorphic to ⊕_i Top(G_i). This uses graded pieces; replacing them by the nested P_i repeats the highest slope and is false.

items.name: Generic PBQ filtration commutes with local extension
items.statement: Mη is PBQ iff Eα⊗Mη is PBQ, and the generic PBQ filtration extends to the PBQ filtration over Eα.

items.name: PBQ over bounded-disc and dagger rings
items.statement: A φ–∇ module over K[[x]]₀ or E† is PBQ iff its E-extension is PBQ. The definition does not identify the bounded quotient over E with a quotient descending to either smaller ring.

items.name: PBQ filtration descends to a bounded-disc lattice
items.statement: The generic PBQ filtration of E⊗K[[x]]₀M₀ is induced by a unique filtration by φ–∇ submodules of M₀. CT11 Theorem 5.6 first descends P₁; Corollary 5.10 iterates.

items.name: PBQ filtration descends to a bounded Robba lattice
items.statement: For M† over E†, the PBQ filtration of its E-extension descends uniquely to φ–∇ submodules of M†. Use Ohkubo's bounded Robba statement, not the full unbounded Robba ring.

items.name: Logarithmic-growth solution filtration
items.statement: For λ≥0 set K[[x]]_λ={Σa_nx^n analytic on |x|<1 : limsup |a_n|/(n+1)^λ<∞}; Sol_λ(M₀) is the space of horizontal K[[x]]₀-linear maps into this module. The derivative is with respect to x on both sides.

items.name: PBQ log-growth and Frobenius comparison
items.statement: For PBQ M₀ over K[[x]]₀ with maximal generic Frobenius slope λmax, Sol_λ(M₀)=Sol(M₀)_(≤λ−λmax) for λ≥0. This is the stated special-disc comparison; the E† logarithmic Robba solution version needs its separate coefficient-space definition.

items.name: Bounded solutions of a PBQ disc module
items.statement: For PBQ M₀, Sol₀(M₀)=Sol(M₀)_(−λmax). Evaluation gives the pure quotient L₀=K[[x]]₀⊗K Sol₀(M₀)∨, of slope λmax and rank dim_K Sol₀(M₀). The displayed vector space on the rank's right-hand side requires dim_K.

items.name: PBQ overconvergent coefficient on a curve
items.statement: An overconvergent F-isocrystal M† on smooth connected C/k is PBQ when its generic φ–∇ module is PBQ on a nonempty affine open. This condition is independent of the affine open and all chosen local presentations.

items.statement: Every nonzero irreducible overconvergent F-isocrystal on a smooth connected curve is PBQ, since the global PBQ filtration has only one step.

items.name: Global bounded quotient when slopes exist
items.statement: If the convergent realization M has a slope filtration, its bounded quotient is the convergent quotient ⊕_i Top(G_i), where G_i are the convergent realizations of the graded global PBQ pieces. Its generic fiber is Mη/Mη^b; do not assert overconvergence of this quotient.

items.statement: PBQ overconvergent curve coefficients of the same maximal generic slope have PBQ direct sum.

items.name: Nonzero curve quotients preserve PBQ slope
items.statement: A nonzero overconvergent quotient of a PBQ curve coefficient is PBQ and has the same maximal generic slope.

items.name: PBQ and finite étale curve maps
items.statement: For finite étale f:C′→C between smooth connected curves, a PBQ N† on C pulls back to a PBQ f* N†; if the direct image f_*M† of M† on C′ is PBQ then M† is PBQ. Correct the printed base assignments. The printed proof of the first implication needs a noncircular replacement, recorded as a gap.

items.name: Globalizing unit-root local lattices
items.statement: A unit-root generic φ–∇ module with a bounded-disc lattice at every interior closed point and an Eα† lattice at every boundary point comes from a unit-root overconvergent F-isocrystal, unique up to isomorphism. Katz correspondence and finite local monodromy supply the descent.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Globalizing subobjects by interior and boundary lattices
items.statement: For an overconvergent curve M†, a generic submodule Lη with compatible bounded-disc lattices inside M at interior points and dagger lattices at boundary points is induced by a unique overconvergent subobject L†⊂M†. For rank r use its determinant line and recover it as the kernel of wedge with that line.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Kummer-twisted Legendre PBQ example
items.statement: For p odd, C=P¹_Fp\{0,1,∞}, let L† be first relative rigid cohomology of the Legendre elliptic family y²=x(x−1)(x−z), and twist by the quadratic character from w²=z(z−1). For p≡1 mod 4 and the unit root π_p of y²=x³−x, the source constructs a nonsplit extension 0→L†(χ)→M†→1(π_p²)→0 with maximal generic slopes 1 and 0 and two PBQ steps. Its cohomological K3 calculation and existence proof remain G4 in this checkpoint; this is not a self-extension.

items.name: Local saturation by the maximal-slope quotient
items.statement: M† over E† is saturated iff its canonical E†-linear map M†→Top(E⊗M†) is injective. This is a condition on a differential Frobenius module, not torsion-freeness of a quotient of lattices.

items.name: Quasi-saturated embedding
items.statement: For pure nonzero M over E, an injective horizontal Frobenius E†-map N†→M is quasi-saturated if its image spans M over E. The datum includes this embedding, not just the abstract module.

items.name: Image in a pure target is a dagger differential Frobenius module
items.statement: For nonzero compatible θ†:N†→M pure, its E†-linear image is a nonzero φ–∇ module; Frobenius and connection descend. Consequently every irreducible N† is saturated.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Injection into a pure target identifies maximal slope
items.statement: If θ†:N†→M is injective with M pure and θ† compatible with ∇ and Frobenius, then λmax(N)=slope(M), by applying PBQ quotient stability to the first PBQ piece.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Image rank bound and equality criterion
items.statement: If the E-linearized θ:N→M is surjective and L†=im θ†, then L† is quasi-saturated and rank Top(L)≥rank M. Equality makes Top(L)→M an isomorphism and L† saturated.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Local saturation quotient
items.statement: Define M^(sat,†) as the image of M†→Top(M). It has the same maximal-slope quotient, is saturated, and M†→M^(sat,†) is an isomorphism when M† was saturated. This construction is a quotient, not an enlargement of M†.

items.name: Quasi-saturated implies saturated
items.statement: For a quasi-saturated N†→M with pure M, rank Top(N)=rank M and N† is saturated. This is Theorem 2.14 applied with all embedding hypotheses retained.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Local irreducibility criterion
items.statement: A nonzero N† over E† is irreducible iff it is PBQ, saturated and Top(N) is irreducible over E.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Local recovery of saturated graded PBQ pieces
items.statement: An isomorphism N/N^b≅M/M^b yields equal PBQ lengths and a unique compatible isomorphism between the direct sums of saturations of the graded PBQ pieces of N† and M†. It does not reconstruct extension classes between distinct graded pieces.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Strong local maximal-slope lifting
items.statement: For M†,N† over E† and h:Top(N)→Top(M), assume either both are irreducible and h≠0, or both are PBQ and saturated and h is an isomorphism. Then a unique isomorphism g†:N†→M† induces exactly h.

items.name: Saturation of a variety coefficient
items.statement: For smooth connected separated finite-type X/k, M† is saturated if on every nonempty affine open U where its convergent realization has a slope filtration, the map from overconvergent sections to the top convergent quotient's sections is injective.

items.name: Saturation can be checked on one affine dense open
items.statement: The condition in Definition 5.1 is equivalent to injectivity for one suitable affine dense open V. Use the actual v3 proof with image control and flat Frobenius; mere generic vector-space injection is insufficient.

items.name: Overconvergent image of the top-quotient section map
items.statement: On an affine smooth lift with a slope-filtered convergent realization, the image of the dagger section module in the top convergent quotient is a finite dagger module with integrable connection and horizontal Frobenius, hence an overconvergent quotient. Noetherianity, faithful flatness and Berthelot's criterion are substantive inputs.

items.name: Dense restriction preserves and detects saturation
items.statement: M† is saturated on X iff its restriction to any nonempty open U is saturated.

items.name: Irreducible overconvergent variety coefficients are saturated
items.statement: A nonzero irreducible overconvergent F-isocrystal on smooth connected X is saturated; restrict to a slope-filtered open, form the image, and use full faithfulness and extension of subobjects.

items.name: Saturation under finite étale pullback
items.statement: For a finite étale morphism f:X′→X of smooth connected varieties, M† is saturated iff f* M† is saturated, using faithfully flat affine section maps.

items.name: Saturation under finite coefficient extension and Frobenius iteration
items.statement: Under the finite coefficient/residue extension and positive Frobenius iterate of Appendix B, M† is saturated iff its pullback is saturated. The proof compares slope filtrations and injectivity after faithful scalar extension.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Canonical saturation quotient on a variety
items.statement: Every overconvergent F-isocrystal M† has a saturated quotient M^(sat,†) whose canonical maps to the maximal-slope quotient agree on every slope-filtered affine dense open. Construct on such an open and extend the quotient via the overconvergent subobject-extension theorem; no global slope filtration is assumed for this construction.

items.name: Dense restriction and extension of overconvergent subobjects
items.statement: For the smooth varieties and dense open immersions used here, overconvergent restriction is fully faithful, and a subobject of the restriction of a global overconvergent coefficient extends globally in the cited source scope. These are distinct input statements; precise proofs and generality remain G3.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Overconvergent-to-convergent full faithfulness
items.statement: The forgetful functor from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals is fully faithful in Kedlaya's smooth-variety setting. It is not asserted essentially surjective.

items.name: Curve quasi-saturation rank equality
items.statement: Let M≠0 be a pure convergent curve coefficient, N† overconvergent with slope-filtered N, and N→M surjective. If the induced map of overconvergent N† sections into convergent M sections is injective on one affine dense open, then λmax(N)=slope(M) and rank Top(N)=rank M.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Boundary kernel's maximal PBQ piece descends
items.statement: With H=ker(N→M), the local dagger kernel Hα† may be smaller after completion than Hα. The local quasi-saturation theorem identifies their maximal-slope quotient ranks; their maximal PBQ submodules then agree after completion. This supplies the boundary lattices needed to globalize the maximal PBQ subobject of H and contradict section injectivity.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Curve irreducibility criterion
items.statement: For a nonzero overconvergent curve coefficient whose convergent realization has a slope filtration, irreducibility is equivalent to PBQ, saturation and irreducibility of its top convergent quotient.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Extensions with smaller subobject slope
items.statement: For 0→L†→M†→N†→0 on a curve, with irreducible ends and s_L<s_N, M† is not saturated; the extension is nonsplit iff M† is PBQ. Use a dense slope-filtered open when necessary.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Equal-slope extensions
items.statement: With the same irreducible-end hypotheses and s_L=s_N, M† is PBQ and saturated, Top(M) is reducible, and the original extension is nonsplit iff the induced top-quotient extension is nonsplit.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Extensions with larger subobject slope
items.statement: If s_L>s_N, the two-step extension is the PBQ filtration and is nonsplit iff M† is saturated. If additionally rank M†=2, it splits by convergent splitting and global full faithfulness; do not extend this rank-two conclusion indiscriminately.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Global recovery of saturated graded PBQ pieces
items.statement: For slope-filtered convergent realizations M,N on a smooth connected curve, an isomorphism of convergent bounded quotients N/N^b→M/M^b determines a unique compatible isomorphism of the sums of saturated graded PBQ pieces of N† and M†, with equal PBQ lengths.

items.name: Strong maximal-slope lifting on curves
items.statement: For smooth connected C over perfect k, M†,N† over K with slope-filtered convergent realizations and h:Top(N)→Top(M), assume either irreducibility of both and h≠0, or both PBQ and saturated and h invertible. Then there is a unique isomorphism N†→M† inducing h.

items.name: Weaker maximal-quotient hypothesis suffices
items.statement: The curve lifting conclusion still holds if specified quotients Top(M),Top(N) are isoclinic and all slopes of their kernels at every point are strictly smaller. Shrink to a dense open with full slope filtrations and extend the resulting morphism by dense full faithfulness.

items.name: Dual minimal-slope formulation
items.statement: Dualizing the maximal-quotient theorem yields the curve minimal-slope theorem for the increasing filtration's minimal-slope subobjects. Reverse both arrow direction and slope sign under duality; compatibility with the specified morphism is part of the curve conclusion.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Lefschetz condition through a closed point
items.statement: For irreducible M† and closed α∈X, LC means a smooth curve Cα→X with a kα-rational point over α such that its pullback of M† remains irreducible. Curves chosen for two coefficients need not be the same.

items.name: Curve lift when the target stays irreducible
items.statement: For nonzero h:Top(N)→Top(M), slope-filtered realizations, irreducible M† and LC for M† through α, the maximal PBQ subobject of N† restricted to the chosen curve has a unique compatible surjection to the restricted M†.

items.name: Curve lift when the source stays irreducible
items.statement: For the corresponding hypotheses with N† irreducible and LC for N†, its restriction to the chosen curve has a unique compatible injection into the maximal PBQ subobject of the restricted M†.

items.name: Closed fibers identified by two Lefschetz curves
items.statement: If both M† and N† are irreducible and satisfy LC at α, the two independent rank inequalities force equal ranks and an isomorphism of their F-spaces over Kα. A common irreducibility-preserving curve is not required.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Unit-root source gives a compatible global surjection
items.statement: In Proposition 6.7's setting, if M† is irreducible, LC holds at one closed point, and N† is unit-root, then M† is unit-root and there is a unique overconvergent surjection N†→M† inducing h.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Finite coefficient-field structure
items.statement: In §7 only, k=Fq, K=Frac W(k), σ=id. For finite L/K⊂Qpbar, an L-coefficient overconvergent Fq-isocrystal is an ordinary coefficient with a unital K-algebra map L→End_F(M†); morphisms commute with that action. This is not merely tensoring every object with L.

items.name: Tensor product with coefficient projector
items.statement: For Li-objects and L=L₁L₂, tensor the underlying coefficients and apply −⊗_(L₁⊗K L₂)L via multiplication. The induced connection and Frobenius are horizontal; normalized rank rank_K/[L:K] is the product of the two normalized ranks.

items.statement: Equip the underlying K-dual with action (a·η)(m)=η(am). Via the nondegenerate field-trace pairing identify it with the L-linear dual and define the L-valued evaluation/coevaluation after the coefficient projector. items.statement: Take the filtered 2-colimit of finite L-coefficient categories along θ. Objects and morphisms have finite fields of definition. Define Qpbar-rank as rank_K M/[L:K], independent of representative; scalar extension, tensor and dual descend through the colimit.

items.name: Underlying coefficient of an absolutely irreducible object is isotypic
items.statement: If an irreducible Qpbar-coefficient object is represented by an L-object, its underlying K-coefficient is a direct sum of finitely many copies of one irreducible overconvergent F-isocrystal. It need not itself be irreducible.

items.name: Changing the finite base field's Frobenius convention
items.statement: For k₀⊂k of degree n and q=q₀^n, form ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1}(F_q₀^i)*M† with cyclic Frobenius closing by F_M. The Li-action is σ₀^i-twisted on the i-th summand when the chosen coefficient field carries σ₀. The resulting Qpbar-coefficient equivalence has unchanged normalized rank.

items.name: Finite constant-field pullback and pushforward
items.statement: For k_n/k of degree n and K_n/K unramified, Qpbar-coefficient pullback combines geometric base extension, nth Frobenius iterate and the projector identifying the two K_n actions. Pushforward is restriction with the cyclic induction. Normalized ranks are unchanged by pullback and multiplied by n by pushforward.

items.name: Rigid cohomology with finite-field coefficient action
items.statement: For separated finite-type X/k and overconvergent L-coefficient M†, ordinary and compactly supported rigid cohomology carry L-linear Frobenius. Form these from actual frame/de Rham cohomology, not an axiom of finite-dimensional output.

items.name: Cohomological base change with coefficient projector
items.statement: For L⊃K_n, H^i(X_n/K_n,π_n* M†) is the projected base change of H^i(X/K,M†), identified as an L-space with the original cohomology carrying F^n and K_n action from L; the same holds for compact supports.

items.name: Linearized closed-point Frobenius
items.statement: At closed α of degree n, apply the coefficient projector to the fiber after Kα-extension and use the nth iterate of q-Frobenius. The resulting L-linear F_{α} has a characteristic polynomial independent of enlarging L; its degree is the normalized rank.

items.name: Fiber trace under rational-point and coefficient changes
items.statement: The projected fiber agrees with the underlying L-space carrying the iterated operator; different k_n-rational lifts are Frobenius conjugate and have equal traces. Restriction of scalars gives Tr_K(T)=Tr_{L/K}(Tr_L T)=Σ_{τ:L→Qpbar over K}τ(Tr_L T). Use splitting after Qpbar-extension, not L⊗K L as a product without normality.

items.name: Rigid Lefschetz trace formula over coefficient fields
items.statement: For connected separated finite-type pure-d X/Fq and every n>0, Σ_{β∈X(F_(q^n))}Tr_L(F_β^n)=Σ_{i=0}^{2d}(−1)^iTr_L(F^n|H_c^i(X/K,M†)), with the stated coefficient linearizations. Excision, the ordinary trace formula and nondegenerate field trace prove the coefficient extension.

items.name: Coefficient L-function
items.statement: L(X,M†,t)=∏_{closed α}det(1−t^degα F_α|M_α)^−1, as a formal series with Qpbar coefficients. It also equals exp(Σ_{n≥1}Σ_{β∈X(F_(q^n))}Tr(F_β^n)t^n/n).

items.name: Cohomological determinant formula
items.statement: L(X,M†,t)=∏_{i=0}^{2d}det(1−tF|H_c^i(X/K,M†))^((−1)^(i+1)), hence is rational. Keep support, Frobenius and twist conventions fixed.

items.name: Iota purity and mixedness
items.statement: Fix a field isomorphism ι:Qpbar→C. A coefficient is ι-pure of real weight w when each closed degree-n Frobenius eigenvalue has absolute value q^(nw/2). It is ι-mixed if it has a finite filtration with pure graded pieces. Arbitrary coefficient objects require real weights; integer-only purity in the preprint conflicts with Theorem 7.18.

items.name: Finiteness of rigid cohomology with Frobenius coefficients
items.statement: For a separated finite-type k-scheme and overconvergent F-isocrystal, H^i and H_c^i are finite dimensional in the source's coefficient range. This is a theorem, not part of the definition of the cohomology object.

items.name: Compact-support Poincaré duality
items.statement: For smooth pure-d X, the rigid pairing H^i(X,M∨)×H_c^(2d−i)(X,M)→K(−d) is perfect with Frobenius compatibility. In particular a q^d eigenvalue on top compact cohomology detects a Frobenius-fixed vector in H⁰ of the dual.

items.name: Compact-support weight bounds
items.statement: For an ι-pure weight-w overconvergent coefficient, H_c^i has weights ≤w+i in the specified algebraic/iota coefficient setting. With Hom coefficient pure weight zero, lower degrees cannot contribute a pole at t=q^(−d); retain source hypotheses rather than infer integrality of w.

items.name: Pure-Hom Chebotarev identification
items.statement: Let X/Fq be smooth connected separated finite type and M†,N† irreducible Qpbar-coefficient objects with N†∨⊗M† ι-pure. If their linearized F-fibers are isomorphic at every closed point of a dense open, then M†≅N†. Equality of local factors, the weight-zero Hom pole and duality yield a nonzero global morphism.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Prescribed morphism from endomorphism-surjectivity
items.statement: In the Chebotarev setting with slope filtrations and a fixed isomorphism h:Top(N)→Top(M), suppose after some finite constant-field extension the map End(M†)→End(Top(M)) or the corresponding map for N† is surjective. Then there is a unique compatible overconvergent isomorphism inducing h. Trace averaging must use the projected coefficient normalization.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Lefschetz condition with Qpbar coefficients
items.statement: LC_Qpbar asks for a smooth curve through the specified closed point on which the Qpbar-coefficient object remains irreducible. This is stronger than choosing a curve preserving a particular reducible underlying K-object's rank.

items.name: Lefschetz fibers imply global isomorphism
items.statement: If both irreducible coefficients satisfy LC_Qpbar at every closed point of a dense open, have slope filtrations and pure Hom coefficient, and h between their top quotients is nonzero, they are isomorphic. With the finite-extension endomorphism-surjectivity condition, the isomorphism inducing h is unique.

items.name: Faithfulness of restriction of endomorphisms
items.statement: For connected X and nonempty Y→X in the stated coefficient setting, restriction injects End(M†) into End(f* M†), and likewise for the top convergent quotient. Horizontal sections are detected at a fiber; this is not a surjectivity statement.

items.name: Curve endomorphism preservation controls the top quotient
items.statement: If a smooth curve through α preserves irreducibility of M† and restriction End(M†)→End(M†|C) is bijective, then End(M†)→End(Top(M)) is bijective. Combine restriction injections with the strong curve theorem.
items.note: Proposed Part II, not an existing accepted stage; source and proof gates below remain open.

items.name: Abe–Esnault mixedness and irreducible purity
items.statement: On smooth connected separated finite-type X/Fq every overconvergent Qpbar-coefficient object is ι-mixed, and an irreducible one is ι-pure after allowing arbitrary real weights. The determinant-normalizing rank-one twist must be restored, not silently forced to integer weight.

items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Abe–Esnault irreducibility-preserving curves
items.statement: For irreducible overconvergent Qpbar coefficient M† on smooth connected X/Fq there is a dense open U such that every closed point of U lies on a smooth curve mapping to X whose pullback of M† is irreducible. AE supplies a stronger finite-set version; the one-point version suffices here.

items.name: Higher-dimensional minimal-slope isomorphism
items.statement: For smooth connected separated finite-type X/Fq and irreducible overconvergent Qpbar coefficients M†,N† whose convergent realizations have slope filtrations, a nonzero h:Top(N)→Top(M) implies an overconvergent isomorphism N†≅M†. This conclusion alone does not say it induces the specified h.

items.name: Compatible higher-dimensional lift under curve endomorphism condition
items.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, assume after a finite constant extension a smooth curve through a closed point preserves irreducibility of M† and induces a bijection End(M†)→End(M†|C). Then the global isomorphism can be chosen to induce the given h; the intermediate lifting theorem supplies uniqueness.

items.name: Finite fixed coefficient field
items.statement: For a complete mixed-characteristic discrete valuation field K admitting q-Frobenius σ, Kσ is a finite extension of Qp with residue cardinal ≤q.

items.name: Unramified extension aligning fixed coefficients
items.statement: After a finite unramified extension K′/K carrying σ, its fixed field has residue Fq and the same valuation group as K. For perfect residue k′, K′≅(K′)σ⊗W(Fq)W(k′), with σ acting by Witt q-Frobenius.

items.name: Enlarging Frobenius coefficients to contain a finite p-adic field
items.statement: For finite L/Qp there are finite K′/K and n>0 such that σ extends, the residue of (K′)^(σ^n) is F_(q^n), and L⊂(K′)^(σ^n). The displayed construction id_L⊗σ over K^(σ^n) needs a compatibility repair; retain this theorem as source-stated with G6, not as a closed proof.

items.name: Tubes and strict neighborhoods
items.statement: For a frame X⊂X̄⊂P over R, the tube ]Z[ is sp^−1(Z) in the rigid generic fiber; j† is the colimit over strict neighborhoods of ]X[ in ]X̄[. The specialization map points from the rigid generic fiber to the special fiber.

items.name: Frobenius lift extends to strict neighborhoods

items.name: Affine realization equivalence with Frobenius
items.statement: For affine smooth X with chosen dagger lift and Frobenius, global sections give the equivalence between overconvergent F-isocrystals and finite projective dagger modules with integrable K-connection and horizontal linearized Frobenius, in Berthelot's precise setting. The proof supplies overconvergence of the connection from Frobenius.

items.name: Raw coefficient extension and Frobenius iteration
items.statement: For a finite extension L/K with compatible q-Frobenius and integer n>0, pull back X to the residue extension, extend scalars to L and replace F by F^n. Record n independently from [L:K]; they need not be equal.

items.name: Cyclic induction with restriction of scalars
items.statement: For an L-object with σ^n-Frobenius, pushforward is the K-object ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1}(ϕ^i)*π_*N with cyclic Frobenius whose last transition is F_N. This is right adjoint to the raw pullback; its K-rank is multiplied by n[L:K].

items.name: Adjunction unit and Frobenius trace
items.statement: The unit sends m to (m,F^−1m,…,F^(−n+1)m). The trace sends (a_i⊗m_i)_i to Σ_i tr_(L/K)(σ^i(a_i))F^i(1⊗m_i); both maps are horizontal and Frobenius-equivariant.

items.name: Trace-unit degree and tower laws
items.statement: For the raw functors Tr∘ad=n[L:K]·id. For towers K⊂L⊂M and Frobenius iterates m,n, pullback, pushforward, unit and trace compose in the displayed order. Projected Qpbar-coefficient functors of §7 have a different rank normalization, which must be derived explicitly before averaging.

items.name: Pure slope boundedness after normalization
items.statement: Every pure φ–∇ module over Eη or Eα is bounded: use an allowed finite coefficient extension and Frobenius iterate to twist to unit-root, then descend boundedness. This strengthens Proposition 3.9(2), whose printed hypothesis is unit-root.

items.name: Union of well-ordered supports
items.statement: If I,J⊂Q are well-ordered then I∪J is well-ordered, by the pinned Set.IsPWO.union under a linear order.

items.name: Sum of well-ordered supports
items.statement: If I,J⊂Q are well-ordered then I+J is well-ordered. The additive theorem Set.IsPWO.add is generated by the read to_additive declaration IsPWO.mul.

items.name: Positive support has well-ordered additive closure
items.statement: For well-ordered I⊂Q>0, the union of the positive iterated sums of I is well-ordered. The pinned Set.IsPWO.addSubmonoid_closure even allows nonnegative generators, and restriction to positive-length sums is by subset.

items.name: Algebraic closure of the divisible residue Hahn field
items.statement: For algebraically closed k and the divisible ordered group Q, the Hahn field k((t^Q)) is algebraically closed. The proof is an external Kaplansky/Kedlaya input; the HahnSeries carrier in Mathlib does not itself supply this theorem.

items.name: Cyclic vector for the relevant Frobenius difference module
items.statement: For the E† and Ẽ† difference fields with the monomial Frobenius and characteristic-zero coefficients used in §2, the finite-dimensional φ-module admits a cyclic vector after the source's permitted reductions. Read the exact cited hypotheses before generalizing to arbitrary endomorphisms.

items.name: Unit-root generic coefficient and p-adic representation
items.statement: A unit-root generic F-space in the source coefficient setting corresponds to a continuous representation of G_(k(C)) over Kσ; interior bounded-disc lattices imply unramifiedness at interior points. Exact equivalence and descent hypotheses are a source gate, not supplied by bare local-monodromy theory.

items.name: Unit-root dagger lattice implies finite local monodromy
items.statement: In the unit-root representation correspondence, an Eα†-lattice yields finite local monodromy at the boundary. This is stronger than a statement that arbitrary Frobenius differential modules become unipotent after extension.
items.note: The owning existing layer covers this direction, but no exact declaration-level provider was located; route as an additional located source, not as a built theorem.

items.name: Overconvergent unit-root coefficients from finite boundary monodromy
items.statement: A continuous Kσ-representation unramified on C and with finite local monodromy at the omitted boundary points corresponds to a unit-root overconvergent F-isocrystal in the cited curve setting.
